Three Cardinals prospects to watch for possible 2027 Major League debuts
Thirteen Cardinals prospects debuted in Major League Baseball during 2026. With strong performances by Rainiel Rodriguez, Liam Doyle, and Tanner Franklin highlighted by team officials, more debuts could follow in 2027.
The St. Louis Cardinals' farm system saw thirteen players make their Major League debuts in 2026, with several top prospects showing promise at the highest level, according to an Oct. 15 newsletter excerpt from Will Leitch.
The organization is expected to continue introducing new talent in 2027, as both existing prospects and recent draft picks have progressed. MLB Pipeline’s Jim Callis described the Cardinals’ 2026 Draft class as the most impressive in the league, and when Pipeline ranked all thirty farm systems in August, St. Louis was listed fourth.
Among those being closely watched are Rainiel Rodriguez, Liam Doyle, and Tanner Franklin. Rodriguez, a catcher signed out of the Dominican Republic for $300,000 in April 2024, posted a .324/.413/.574 batting line over 115 games between High-A Peoria and Double-A Springfield during the 2026 season. While he is considered a serviceable catcher, his defensive future remains uncertain due to competition from Leo Bernal—who debuted in September—and ongoing training at first and third base.
Liam Doyle was selected fifth overall by St. Louis in the first round of the 2025 Draft. The left-handed pitcher rebounded from a slow start to finish strong with a 1.63 ERA across his final outings—including postseason appearances—and recorded seventy-three strikeouts over sixty and two-thirds innings during that stretch.
Tanner Franklin, another pick from the 2025 Draft (seventy-second overall), accumulated one hundred thirty-three strikeouts across one hundred five innings between High-A and Double-A this year. He started Game One of Springfield's Texas League Championship Series run with six-and-a-third innings pitched and nine strikeouts without issuing any walks.
Both Doyle and Franklin are not expected to reach the Majors until later in the upcoming season, but are seen as key examples of what St. Louis aims to accomplish through its Minor League pitching program.
